expect:
Two marks per piece of evidence (1 for identifying the evidence, 1 for explaining how it supports the hypothesis):
• The Moon's composition closely matches Earth's mantle rather than its core — this is consistent with Theia's impact excavating mantle material and ejecting it into orbit, but not with the Moon forming independently (Co-accretion) or elsewhere (Capture).
• The Moon has a disproportionately small iron core — the iron in Theia would have already sunk into Earth's core before the collision, leaving the ejected debris iron-poor, which matches what we observe. Neither Capture nor Co-accretion predicts this.
• Apollo rock samples have almost identical oxygen isotope ratios to Earth's rocks — this implies the Moon formed from Earth-derived material, consistent with a giant impact but not with capture from a distant origin.
[4 marks — 2 marks per evidence strand]

Interpret the following information about four planetary bodies:

Body W: mass similar to Earth, surface temperature ~460 °C, thick carbon dioxide atmosphere.
Body X: mass 320 × Earth, surface temperature –145 °C, retains hydrogen and helium atmosphere.
Body Y: mass 0.11 × Earth, surface temperature –63 °C, thin carbon dioxide atmosphere.
Body Z: mass 0.015 × Earth, temperature varies from –180 °C to +130 °C, effectively no atmosphere.

expect:
W — cannot retain a thick atmosphere: despite high surface temperature suggesting fast molecular speeds, this body (Venus-like data) actually has a thick atmosphere in reality. Credit for linking low escape velocity on small bodies to atmospheric loss; if candidate notes high temperature → faster molecules → harder to retain, award credit.
X — retains thick atmosphere: very high mass → very high escape velocity; even light molecules (hydrogen, helium) cannot escape. [1 mark for correct reasoning]
Y — thin atmosphere only: moderate mass gives moderate escape velocity; light gases escape but heavier CO₂ is partially retained. [1 mark for correct reasoning]

[3 marks — 1 mark per well-reasoned body, up to 3]
value:
W — retains a thick atmosphere: mass close to Earth's → high escape velocity; heavy molecules such as carbon dioxide stay bound even though the high temperature makes them move fast. [1 mark for correct reasoning]
X — retains thick atmosphere: very high mass → very high escape velocity; even light molecules (hydrogen, helium) cannot escape. [1 mark for correct reasoning]
Y — thin atmosphere only: moderate mass gives moderate escape velocity; light gases escape but heavier CO₂ is partially retained. [1 mark for correct reasoning]
Z — no thick atmosphere: very low mass → very low escape velocity; even heavy gas molecules can exceed escape velocity and escape. [1 mark for correct reasoning]
[3 marks — 1 mark per well-reasoned body, up to 3]
note: F18: the key contradicted itself ('actually has a thick atmosphere in reality') and awarded Body W no mark. Now consistent and worth 1 mark.
